Either pin torch==2.13.0, librosa==0.11.0 and onnxruntime==1.23.*, or always convert input to WAV/FLAC with ffmpeg first and test 2.14.1 yourself.

recommendation_assessment:
The overall direction is sound. Run separation offline, in its own venv, called as a subprocess, using python-audio-separator. Default to the Resurrection BS-RoFormer vocal model, with Kim Mel-Band (MIT) as the license-clean option. The 44.1 kHz separate-then-resample rule, the cache keyed by hash, and making karaoke and de-reverb A/B options all fit this project. The catalog, API names, stem names and file sizes I checked all hold up.

Corrections I would make:
(1) Fix the Python rationale. 3.13 is not blocked: onnx-weekly ships a cp312-abi3 wheel. Keep 3.12 because it is the PR #298 validation environment, not because of onnx-weekly.
(2) Pin the validated stack. A fresh resolve now pulls torch 2.14.1, onnxruntime 1.31 and librosa 1.0.0. The v0.47.0 lock and PR #298 validated torch 2.13.0, librosa 0.11.0 and onnxruntime 1.23. librosa 1.0 dropped the audioread fallback, and audio-separator loads all input through librosa.load, so m4a/AAC sources will fail. Use a constraints file (torch==2.13.0, librosa==0.11.0) or always ffmpeg-convert to 44.1 kHz WAV/FLAC first, then benchmark 2.14.1 before adopting it.
(3) Add diffq's CC BY-NC 4.0 license to the licensing section. It is a mandatory macOS dependency, though only imported by Demucs paths.
(4) The PR #298 timings belong to FT2-bleedless, Karaoke Gabox v2 and Revive. They are the same architectures, so the estimates hold, but the labels are wrong.
(5) Pass use_soundfile=True, or accept int16 output; the default pydub writer quantizes to int16. Remember the input mix is also peak-normalized before demixing.
(6) For vocal-only mode, prefer the karaoke lead stem without de-reverb as the default reference. The recommended mono anvuew variant de-reverbs aggressively. It is GPL-licensed and its harmony-removal behavior is not what the report describes. Make de-reverb strictly opt-in after an A/B on the aligner and the DTW cost.

The fallback ordering is reasonable: demucs-mlx for speed, MSST only if separation bleed is shown to cause alignment errors. I would not adopt mlx-audio-separator as the main path: it has 17 stars, its benchmarks are from February, and it lacks the BS karaoke models.
missed_options: Pin a validated constraints file for the separation venv: torch==2.13.0, librosa==0.11.0, onnxruntime==1.23.*, numpy<2.6. An unpinned install currently resolves librosa 1.0.0, which has no audioread backend, so m4a/AAC inputs to audio-separator fail. Alternatively, normalize every input to 44.1 kHz stereo WAV/FLAC with ffmpeg before calling the separator.

diffq is CC BY-NC 4.0. It is a hard macOS dependency of audio-separator and is used only by the Demucs paths. If the product is ever distributed commercially, use demucs 4.1 / demucs-mlx for Demucs or vendor around it.

Separator(use_soundfile=True) writes float/input-subtype WAVs instead of the default pydub int16 path. Separator(output_single_stem=...) skips writing unneeded stems, e.g. only 'Vocals' from the karaoke pass.

Workaround for samplerate 0.1.0 without --override: its loader tries ctypes find_library('samplerate') first, so `brew install libsamplerate` plus DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/homebrew/lib also fixes the VR-arch import.

bs_roformer_karaoke_anvuew.ckpt (GPL-3.0, in the audio-separator catalog). Community reports say it extracts lead better on some tracks and handles radio-effect vocals that frazer/becruily misses. It is worth a per-song A/B for K-pop vocal effects.

Near-real-time separation of the LIVE input, as a possible third tracking mode for a live band rather than the original MR. One option is overlapping 1-2 s windows through demucs-mlx (about 100x realtime), which adds window latency. Dedicated low-latency models (HS-TasNet, about 23 ms latency) score only about 4.6-5.5 dB on MUSDB and have no verified public code. This is probably not worth it initially, but it is the only way to compare vocal against vocal when the live input is a full mix with different instrumentation.

Faster, higher-SDR checkpoints exist that are not in the catalog yet. unwa's bs_resurrection2_quality_test (11.66 on Multisong) and Leap Xe (11.76-11.79) are both dim-256-class BS models, usable via MSST in a separate venv. Only pursue them if alignment errors trace back to bleed.

torch.compile results on MPS: fp32+compile beats autocast and autocast+compile for warm runs (Kim 18.0 s vs 21.3 s). For a long-running prep worker that keeps one Separator alive, fp32+compile is the faster mode. For one-shot CLI runs, autocast eager avoids compile warm-up.
